claims: The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines for managing dyslipidemia replace the 2018 guidelines.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines include an LDL-C goal of <100 mg/dL for intermediate-risk individuals.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines include an LDL-C goal of <70 mg/dL for high-risk individuals.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines include an LDL-C goal of <55 mg/dL for very high-risk atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) patients.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines reintroduce specific LDL-C and non-HDL-C targets rather than relying solely on percentage reductions.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines use the AHA PREVENT-ASCVD equations for risk assessment in primary prevention.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines recommend LDL-C <55 mg/dL for patients with ASCVD at very high risk.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines give a 2a recommendation for addition of ezetimibe if LDL-C remains ≥100 mg/dL on max statins for severe hypercholesterolemia with LDL-C 190 mg/dL or higher.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines recommend measuring Lp(a) at least once in adulthood to assess risk.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines expand use of noncontrast CAC scans for men >40 and women >45 with borderline or intermediate risk.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines state that a CAC score ≥100 supports an LDL-C goal <70 mg/dL.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines state that a CAC score ≥300 supports an optional LDL-C goal <55 mg/dL.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines use Apolipoprotein B (ApoB) to assess residual risk, especially in patients with high triglycerides or diabetes.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines define high-intensity statin as ≥50% LDL-C reduction with atorvastatin 40–80 mg and rosuvastatin 20–40 mg.
The 2026 ACC/AHA guidelines define moderate-intensity statin as 30%–49% reduction with atorvastatin 10–20 mg, rosuvastatin 5–10 mg, and simvastatin 20–40 mg.
